uniqueness.qualified_wording: `store.producer_is_model` is the only *scalar bare-literal model-standing comparison* in `src/resextract` -- the only place that decides model standing by testing a single producer value against the `"model"` literal. It is NOT the only place `"model"` is spelled, and NOT the only producer comparison overall (`docket/assemble.py:1690` compares against the second vocabulary `"mixed"`).
uniqueness.declaration_vs_comparison_criterion: A *declaration site* spells the producer literal because the vocabulary must be written down somewhere -- `PRODUCER_VOCAB` (store.py:54), `MODEL_PRODUCER` (store.py:57), the SQL CHECKs (store.py:489/536/538), and the five functions that *return* a producer string (decompose.py:329, assess/evidence.py:271, mine/candidates.py:356, llm/occamy.py:777, docket/materialize.py:563). A declaration *establishes* a value and duplicates no decision rule, so it is legitimate and expected and is NOT a counterexample to uniqueness. A *comparison* re-derives the model-standing decision by testing a value against the literal; that IS the rule, and duplicating it is what creates drift risk. Only scalar bare-literal model-standing comparisons count against the claim.
